implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py builds a 3x3 grid of tk.Buttons in _build_grid(); tictactoegui.py does the same.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players alternate turns using symbols X and O
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.__init__ creates two Player objects with symbols "X" and "O"; Game.play_move switches player after a successful move.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Move validation (cannot place on occupied cell)
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_valid_move and Board.make_move reject invalid indices; Game.play_move returns False if board.make_move fails; GUI ignores the click.
Board.check_winner iterates over WINNING_LINES and returns status "win"; Game updates status, winner, and winning_line accordingly.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Draw detection when board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full and Board.check_winner return status "draw" when no empty cells remain; Game records draw.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Status display showing whose turn it is, win or draw messages
implemented_requirements.evidence: TicTacToeGUI._refresh updates status_label text based on Game.status; also shows messagebox on win/draw.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Scoreboard tracking wins for X, O and draws
implemented_requirements.evidence: TicTacToeGUI maintains self.score dict, updates it on win/draw, and displays via score_label.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Controls for starting a new round and resetting scores
implemented_requirements.evidence: TicTacToeGUI._build_control_bar creates "New Round" and "Reset Scores" buttons linked to _new_round and _reset_scores.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ability to input player names (optional but user‑friendly)
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py defines ask_player_names which uses tkinter.simpledialog to ask for names, falling back to defaults.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Highlight the winning line on the board
implemented_requirements.evidence: TicTacToeGUI._highlight_winning_line sets background of winning cells to "light green".

judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete, functional tic‑tac‑toe game with a Tkinter GUI. Core mechanics (3x3 grid, turn‑taking, move validation, win/draw detection) are present in board.py and game.py, while the GUI in gui.py (used by main.py) offers a user‑friendly interface, status updates, score tracking, new‑round and reset controls, and visual highlighting of the winning line. The code appears ready to run, giving a high functional completeness and executable likelihood.
